title: El Niño is dramatically increasing sea levels – how bad could it get? | New Scientist
description: El Niño has already raised sea levels in part of the eastern Pacific by 40 centimetres and as it continues to strengthen, there could be coastal flooding from Alaska to Chile
author: Michael Le Page

title: Archaeologists are uncovering the meaning of a unique rock art site | New Scientist
description: Excavations in the Côa valley in Portugal, the world’s largest site of Palaeolithic open-air rock art, are yielding clues about how engravings of animals were seen by prehistoric hunter-gatherers
author: Benjamin Taub

title: Noise-cancelling headphones prevent vomiting after surgery | New Scientist
description: Nausea and vomiting are common after surgery, which may be partly related to the noises patients are exposed to, even under general anaesthetic. Wearing noise-cancelling headphones while on the operating table reduces the risk
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Japan is launching a mission to Mars’s largest moon Phobos | New Scientist
description: The Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft, set to launch on 20 October, will bring back samples that should solve a moon mystery that has been vexing scientists for more than a century
author: Leah Crane

title: El Niño has killed hundreds of children in Sudan | New Scientist
description: Drought driven by El Niño is causing hunger and disease in Sudan that has already killed hundreds of children
author: Alec Luhn

title: Scientists have just voted to abolish leap seconds | New Scientist
description: Since 1972, officials have added 27 leap seconds to the universal clock, but in a meeting this week in France they have decided to abandon the practice
author: Jo Marchant
